books.section: A. Farmers and the Populist Party
The Silver Issue and the Populist Movement

primary_sources: Frank Leslie's Illustrated Newspaper, 'The People's Party Convention - Delegates Who Were Not In It,' 1892

stimulus.text: Political cartoon, Frank Leslie’s Illustrated Newspaper, 1892, “The People’s Party Convention—Delegates Who Were Not In It.” At the top left, a group is labeled “A Mixed Delegation.” At the right, a tall figure with his back turned is labeled “Farmers Alliance.” In the center, two men shake hands under the label “Lobby Debate.” In the foreground, a man sleeps on the floor, captioned “Away from the Excitement.”
stimulus.source_note: Frank Leslie’s Illustrated Newspaper, 1892, “The People’s Party Convention—Delegates Who Were Not In It.” Public domain: cartoon published 1892 (pre-1930); Library of Congress, LCCN2004677367. Labels checked against the image.

stem: What does the back-turned figure labeled 'Farmers Alliance' suggest?

options.text: The Alliance had already taken over the People's Party completely
options.misconception: A back-turned figure stands apart, not in command of the party.

options.text: The Alliance opposed all political action by farmers everywhere
options.misconception: The Alliance was a political movement; the figure shows division, not opposition to politics.

options.text: The Alliance sent the largest delegation to the Omaha convention
options.misconception: The figure stands outside the convention, not inside it as a delegate.

options.text: Even the farmers' own movement was divided about the new party

rationales.A: Turning his back shows distance, not control of the party.
rationales.B: Alliance members built the party; the question is why some held back.
rationales.C: The cartoon places him outside, among those who were not in it.
rationales.D: His turned back shows that not all Alliance farmers joined the party.
rationales.general:
Read the figure's posture, not just its label.
1. The tall figure wears the label 'Farmers Alliance.'
2. He stands with his back turned to the convention scene.
3. A back turned means distance, not support.
4. Background from the books: many Alliance leaders split over leaving the old parties.
Remember: in a cartoon, a turned back means a group holding itself apart.
